steps.title: Eleven areas
steps.text: Dallasites place a neighbourhood by its part of town: North Dallas, Oak Cliff, East Dallas, Pleasant Grove and more, with downtown at the centre. The freeways, I-30, I-35E, US 75 and the LBJ, are how most people find their way.

steps.title: ZIP codes and known-as names
steps.text: Dallas has no official neighbourhood map, so the map compares ZIP codes, the units the Census counts. The names in italics are the neighbourhoods people actually say, like Bishop Arts, Lakewood or Uptown.

steps.title: School districts
steps.text: A Dallas address doesn't mean Dallas ISD. The city spreads over more than a dozen independent school districts, Richardson, Plano and Garland among them. Tap any spot and the card names the one it's in.

steps.title: Getting around
steps.text: DART's light rail meets downtown and runs out to the suburbs; the Silver Line and the TRE commuter train cross the region, to DFW Airport and Fort Worth. Most of the region still drives.

steps.title: Tap anywhere
steps.text: Tap any spot or search an address, and the card shows the boundaries it falls in, collection day, what living there is like, transit nearby, where to vote and who represents it. Compare puts two places side by side.
